title: sock login: Safari cannot reach 127.0.0.1 callback after Apple sign-in, CLI silent
description: Guy's 50l chain (for i in 1 2 3; do d=$(mktemp -d); XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$d sock login && XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$d sock logout; done): Apple sign-in completed, Safari then could not connect to 127.0.0.1:61006/callback, so the listener that owned the port was gone. Terminal output unknown. Hypotheses: (a) duplicate callback after the one-shot listener closed (double form_post or stale tab), benign but looks like failure; (b) iteration exited early; (c) timeout shorter than the sign-in. Verified: listener works for a single login. Need: failing test first (internal/login, internal/cli/session.go), then make a missed callback loud: say so on stderr instead of nothing. Server logs for the last 3h show no cli-login lines.
notes: Chained loop not reproducible serially (Guy 2026-10-13: 3 serial logins clean). Likely stale tab hitting closed one-shot listener. Added 'sock: sign-in received' on stderr at callback (commit above). Errors on early exit already print via main.

title: Human CLI: sock login (Sign in with Apple via browser handoff) and every human action in the CLI
description: Decided 2026-10-11: humans use CLIs too; every command the apps offer must exist in sock. Today the CLI only acts as a puppet. Login: sock login opens Sign in with Apple in the browser through an Apple Services ID with a redirect to a localhost listener (PKCE/state), exchanges the identity token and authorization code with the hub for a device session token, stores it like the puppet token. Then: registration with invite, terms, profile, handles, devices, puppets (create, list, mint token, erase), conversations, groups, members, send/read, blocks, reports, export, erase account. Needs a contract pass first (Services ID as a second accepted audience in the verifier, CLI device kind, redirect rules), DDD + ADR, security review. Apple side: Services ID creation is a user step.

title: Move the CLI transport (empty token, access gate, ModerationService) and human error texts into sock-client
description: sock-cli-822 needed three things client.New cannot do: skip Authorization when there is no token (login, register), send Sock-Access-Gate to the configured host only, and a ModerationService client. They live in sock-cli internal/cli/clients.go and errors.go as a near copy of client.New's transport. Move them into sock-client so sock-mcp gets the gate too, then delete the CLI copy.
